I have been farming these 5 mu for fifty-five years. I know every piece of this land. My wife and I are the only ones working it now, and at seventy-three, I have to be honest about what my back can handle. Cotton is still my main crop — it has always brought the best money, and I understand it better than anything — but I have cut it down to 2 mu because the spraying and picking are too much for two old people to manage on more land. The other 3 mu I keep in wheat and maize, the rotation every household around here follows: wheat in winter, maize in summer. Wheat gives us flour for the year, and maize is easy money with little work.

For the cotton, I will rotary till in spring and plant improved seed — I buy from the village store, the same kind I have used for years, about 3 jin per mu. I spread one bag of compound fertilizer as basal dressing. I irrigate twice from the well, and I spray for bollworm and weeds about thirteen times — cotton cannot be left alone in this county. I expect about 500 jin per mu.

For wheat, I rotary till after the maize comes off, sow improved seed at 30 jin per mu in October, and put down compound fertilizer as base. At green-up I topdress with some urea. I irrigate three times, including once before winter freeze, and spray two or three times for insects and weeds. I should get around 900 jin per mu.

For maize, I plant hybrid seed directly into the wheat stubble with no-tillage in June — why waste fuel tilling when the stubble is already there? One bag of compound fertilizer is enough. I irrigate twice and spray two or three times. I expect about 800 jin per mu.
